title: Tabletop: Customer Data Leak
context: You are facilitating a tabletop exercise. The scenario: a developer exposed a customer data export in a public repository.

n1.text: First question to ask the group before any technical action?

choices.text: Who decides and what are the pre-established authorities?
choices.why: Preparation defines roles and authorities: it is the first phase.
A late technical detail in a process exercise.

choices.text: What is the price of the repository?

n2.text: The repository is public. Which containment action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Wait for an automatic notification from the provider
Remove the secret, revoke tokens, and restrict repository access
choices.why: Containment aims to stop exposure quickly and reversibly.

n3.text: After stabilization, what must be done as a priority?

choices.text: Close the ticket without a report
choices.why: Closing without lessons learned is a process failure.

choices.text: Document the facts, analyze root cause, and schedule a PIR
choices.why: The post-incident phase captures lessons and feeds playbooks.
The response must be systemic, not punitive.

n4.outcome: A good tabletop identifies gaps in roles, tools, and processes — not a perfect execution.

debrief: Preparation (roles, authorities, playbooks) underpins the entire response.
Containment must be fast and preserve evidence.
PIR and root cause analysis are mandatory before closure.
